name: Carolina Wood Products
old_description: Our website is temporarily unavailable. We are performing scheduled maintenance and will be back online shortly. For orders, quotes, or any questions, please reach out to our team directly. We are open and ready to assist you.
about:
Carolina Wood Products operates from Marshville, North Carolina, where it has manufactured wood pallets and packaging since 1969. The company was founded by Robert and Frances Horne in nearby Peachland before moving to its current Marshville facility. Now in its third generation of family ownership, the business is led by Ronald and Randy Horne, with the next generation, Matt and Randall Horne, recently completing a major sawmill expansion.

The company produces new pallets to GMA standard and custom dimensions, heat-treated pallets certified to ISPM-15 for export, repaired and reconditioned pallets in Grade A and Grade B, as well as custom wooden crates and boxes built to exact specifications. Production relies on automated nailing machines and computerized saws, and a $2.5 million sawmill expansion completed recently added capacity for lumber processing and wood byproducts such as boiler fuel and wood chips. The Marshville facility serves customers across North Carolina, South Carolina, and Georgia.

Customers span manufacturing, food and agriculture, building materials and lumber, distribution and warehousing, export and international shipping, and biomass energy sectors. The company supplies pallets and packaging to businesses in Charlotte, Raleigh, Greensboro, Winston-Salem, Fayetteville, Durham, and throughout the Piedmont and coastal regions.

Carolina Wood Products emphasizes that it is a local manufacturer, not a broker, with every pallet built on-site in Marshville. This vertical integration allows consistent quality, faster turnaround, and direct communication with the production team. The family ownership and recent capital investment reflect a long-term commitment to the region’s supply chain.

name: Carparts of Pepperell
old_description: Carparts Distribution Center is a locally owned and operated automotive parts supplier that has been service the automotive industry since 1975 and many of our employees have been working in the industry for over 40 years.
about:
Carparts Distribution Center, operating as Carparts of Pepperell among other locations, traces its roots to 1975 when it began as a locally owned automotive parts supplier in southern New Hampshire. The company maintains its corporate offices in Plaistow, New Hampshire, while the Pepperell, Massachusetts location serves as one of 21 retail and commercial outlets spread across New Hampshire, Massachusetts, and Maine. Ownership has remained local and private since founding, though the original founders are not named in public records.

The business functions as a full-line automotive parts distributor, stocking replacement components for passenger cars, light trucks, and heavy-duty applications through its Auto Value affiliation. Its network includes 21 storefronts — branded variously as Carparts of [Town], Motor Supply (a division with eight Maine locations), and Steve's Auto Parts — supported by a central distribution center. Each site carries inventory for immediate counter sale and runs commercial delivery routes for professional repair shops, with express and courier options advertised for urgent needs.

Primary customers are independent repair shops, fleet maintenance operations, and do-it-yourself vehicle owners throughout northern New England. The Motor Supply division specifically targets heavy-duty and commercial truck repair in central Maine, while the Carparts-branded locations serve the broader light-vehicle aftermarket across the three-state footprint.

The company positions its longevity and service model as its differentiator, emphasizing that many staff members have spent four decades in the industry. Its internal motto, "SERVICE IS THE DIFFERENCE," reflects a strategy built on in-person counter expertise and rapid local delivery rather than catalog breadth alone.

name: Carpin Manufacturing, Inc.
old_description: Carpin was founded in 1984 as a glide and hardware manufacturing company that immediately became a leader in hardware manufacturing in the office and school furniture industries. Founder Ralph Carpinella, an engineer by education, brought his life-long manufacturing knowledge and furniture industry experience to create a customer-focused company that is based on engineering and innovation.x
about:
Carpin Manufacturing, Inc. was founded in 1984 in Waterbury, Connecticut, by Ralph Carpinella, an engineer who applied his manufacturing expertise to create a glide and hardware company serving the office and school furniture markets. His father, Henry Carpinella, played a key role in the startup and remained involved until his death in 2011, establishing a family-oriented culture that persists today.

The company operates a modern facility near Interstate 84 where it runs progressive and eyelet metal stamping, plastic injection molding, and precision assembly lines. In-house engineering, rapid prototyping, and 3D printing support custom development alongside a catalog of nearly 3,000 stock SKUs, many available for same-day shipment. A stable workforce with an average tenure of 20 years underpins consistent quality and process knowledge.

Carpin supplies floor‑protection products — glides, casters, tubular components, and specialty parts — to schools and universities, commercial and residential office furniture makers, warehouse and factory equipment builders, point‑of‑sale display manufacturers, and medical‑device firms. Notable collaborations include redesigning a side‑chair glide to eliminate field failures for a major office furniture brand and co‑developing a custom caster that matched a task chair’s aesthetic requirements.

The firm emphasizes engineering‑driven problem solving over off‑the‑shelf sales, a philosophy rooted in its founding. Patented glide designs such as the Solo, Smart, Floor Saver, and Simple lines illustrate its focus on proprietary solutions, and the company has been recognized with the James C. Smith Spirit of Excellence Award for its contributions to the industry.

name: Cavist
old_description: Overmolding electronic assemblies yields protection against the harshest environments. Our primary goal is to determine the absolute best way to encapsulate your cable, connector or PCBA, and scale that into volume manufacturing here at Cavist.
about:
Cavist was incorporated in Reno, Nevada, in 1998 by Danish-born founders Kurt Carlson and Reimer Hansen to bring European low-pressure molding technology to the United States. The company began as an equipment developer, introducing the MoldMan line of low-pressure molding machines, before launching a contract manufacturing division in 2008. In 2023, after 26 years of growth, Cavist transitioned to 100% employee ownership.

Today Cavist operates as a contract manufacturer specializing in encapsulating and protecting electronic assemblies. Its core processes include low-pressure molding (LPM), 2-shot overmolding, epoxy overmolding, and cable assembly overmolding, supplemented by turnkey supply services that cover procurement, assembly, testing, and packaging. The 30,000-square-foot facility houses more than 25 injection molding machines and a staff of 35-plus engineers, technicians, and support personnel. Quality systems are certified to ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 13485:2016, and the site includes ISO Class 8 cleanrooms for medical device work.

The company serves automotive, medical, wearable, and defense markets, with customers ranging from individual inventors to Fortune 500 corporations. Automotive programs include sealing for EV and under-hood electronics; medical projects cover implantable and wearable devices requiring biocompatible materials; defense work addresses ruggedized connectors and cable assemblies for harsh environments.

Cavist differentiates itself through 25-plus years of dedicated low-pressure molding experience, in-house moldflow simulation that validates gating and fill before production, and engineering support that begins at the design stage with DFM, material selection, and prototyping. The employee-owned structure is intended to ensure long-term stability and accountability from prototype through high-volume runs.

Engineering support from day one (DFM, material selection, prototyping)

old_description: CCX is proud to be a best in class, North American manufacturer of custom and high speed cables and connectivity solutions. We produce custom cables according to customer specifications as well as high speed fiber, copper and power cables and a complete suite of optics. We do all of this with a friendly and educated team.
about:
CCX Corporation operates from Broomfield, Colorado, drawing on over three decades of cable design and manufacturing experience. The company positions itself as a North American manufacturer of custom and high-speed cables and connectivity solutions, producing custom cables to customer specifications alongside high-speed fiber, copper, power cables, and a full suite of optics. No founding year or founder names are publicly disclosed, and ownership structure is not specified.

The company's capabilities span simple and complex wire harnesses with dozens to hundreds of components, coaxial cable assemblies for 50- and 75-ohm applications including low-loss variants, ribbon assemblies in flat, folded, and color-coded configurations, and custom injection over-molding for strain relief and interconnects. CCX also terminates motor and fan leads, manufactures power cords and adapters certified to UL, cUL, ENEC, VDE, CE, and CCC standards, and builds fiber patch cables (1–144 fibers, OS2/OM1–OM5) in a Class 10k clean room. Copper offerings cover CAT5e through CAT8 in shielded and unshielded versions, plus SAS 3.0 12 Gbps assemblies. The product line extends to compatible optics (SFPs), direct-attach and active optical cables with stateside stocking, and data-center rack integration services.

CCX serves original equipment manufacturers, resellers, and data-center operators. Its customer base includes companies such as Arrow, referenced in a testimonial, and the firm highlights rack-and-stack integration projects for data-center clients. The company markets directly to both OEMs and channel partners through its website.

CCX emphasizes quality-first manufacturing, on-time delivery, and what it describes as unparalleled customer service backed by a friendly, educated team. Differentiators cited include a Class 10k clean room for fiber production, lifetime warranty on optics, TAA-compliant options across power, fiber, and copper lines, and domestic stocking for quick-turn DAC and AOC orders.

name: Center for Composite Materials (CCM)
old_description: The Center for Composite Materials is an internationally recognized Center of Excellence for interdisciplinary research, education, and technology transfer in the areas of materials and synthesis, multifunctional materials, processing science, mechanics and design, sensing and control, and simulation.
about:
The Center for Composite Materials (CCM) was established in 1974 at the University of Delaware in Newark, Delaware. As a university-based research center, it operates under the College of Engineering and draws faculty from multiple departments including mechanical engineering, materials science, and chemical engineering. The center was created to advance interdisciplinary research in composite materials and has since been designated a Center of Excellence eight times by the National Science Foundation and the Department of Defense.

CCM provides a full spectrum of composites research and development services, from material characterization and mechanical testing to process development, prototyping, and component validation. Its 53,688-square-foot facility houses equipment valued at more than $25 million, including autoclaves, resin infusion systems, automated fiber placement, additive manufacturing platforms, and a suite of thermal, mechanical, and nondestructive evaluation instruments. In a recent year, more than 51 faculty members, 41 research professionals and postdoctoral fellows, and 71 graduate and undergraduate students participated in over 50 research projects with annual expenditures exceeding $17 million.

The center serves the automotive, aerospace, defense, and energy sectors. It maintains long-standing collaborations with government agencies such as the Department of Energy, NASA, DARPA, and the U.S. Army’s TARDEC, as well as with industry partners including BAE Systems, major OEMs, and Tier‑1 suppliers. More than 350 companies, ranging from startups to Fortune 500 firms, have engaged with CCM through its University‑Industry Consortium.

CCM distinguishes itself through end-to-end integration of materials science, process engineering, and validation under one roof, enabling rapid translation of laboratory discoveries into manufacturable solutions. Its mission emphasizes technology transfer, workforce development, and the creation of predictive modeling tools that link atomistic physics to composite performance.

about:
Central Laundry Equipment was founded in 1985 in Ward, Arkansas, by Pat and Richard Bradshaw after Richard retired from the U.S. Air Force. The business began in the couple’s living room, moved to a two‑car garage, and now operates from an 18,000‑square‑foot warehouse and office facility. The company remains family‑owned and veteran‑owned.

The firm acts as an authorized distributor for commercial laundry equipment lines including UniMac, Huebsch, Speed Queen, and American Dish Service, as well as Ecolab chemicals. It provides equipment sales, factory‑certified service, a parts department that ships genuine OEM parts within 24 hours, laundry‑room layout and design consulting at no extra charge, lease and rental programs, and on‑site or online resident training. The operation employs over 20 people across Arkansas, Tennessee, and Mississippi.

Customers span hotels, healthcare facilities, correctional institutions, athletic centers, multi‑housing properties, RV parks, truck stops, coin‑operated laundries, fire departments, veterinary clinics, schools, industrial laundries, and linen‑processing plants throughout an eight‑state territory covering Arkansas, Oklahoma, Missouri, Tennessee, Mississippi, Texas, and Louisiana.

The company says its growth is built on personal customer service and value‑added solutions, highlighted by 24/7 live phone support, fully stocked service vehicles, and a commitment to rapid parts fulfillment.

about:
Central Plastics operates from Tracy, California, as a minority- and woman-owned contract development and manufacturing organization. The company does not disclose its founding year or founders publicly.

The firm provides custom plastic injection molding, injection stretch blow molding (ISBM), and custom thermoforming, supported by in-house tooling and engineering. Its facility runs on sustainable energy and houses equipment for scientific molding, prototyping, pilot lots, and commercial-scale continuous production. Value-added services include hot stamping, heat insertion, sonic welding, and assembly.

Central Plastics serves healthcare, aerospace, packaging, defense, consumer, toy and education, and electronics markets. The company emphasizes end-to-end traceability, a metrology lab for first-article inspection, and PPAP levels 1 through 5.

The company differentiates itself through its ISO 13485:2016 and AS9100 Rev D certifications, a cloud-based QMS, and a commitment to diversity and inclusion. It positions itself as an all-in-one provider covering design through production.

about:
Central Textiles Inc operates in Central, South Carolina, where the current owners acquired an existing textile mill in 1984 and embarked on a comprehensive modernization program to create a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility.

The company runs a fully integrated textile operation encompassing spinning, weaving, finishing, and coating and laminating. Its production line includes state-of-the-art air-jet weaving, warping, slashing, carding, and fiber-opening equipment, enabling the manufacture of commercial, industrial, and apparel fabrics as well as technical and industrial textiles.

Central Textiles serves customers in the apparel, commercial, and industrial sectors, supplying fabrics for technical and industrial applications. Finished-goods inquiries are directed to its affiliated company, Cotswold Industries, which handles fabric finishing to customer specifications.

The company emphasizes continuous investment in technology, lean management, and just-in-time processes to reduce waste and cost, positioning itself as a flexible, innovative partner focused on quality, cost efficiency, and adaptability.

Century Seals serves aerospace, defense, refrigeration, gas detection, energetic and pyrotechnic, microwave and RF, electromechanical, and microelectronics sectors. The company describes itself as a preferred source in the microcircuit packaging industry, supplying both standard and custom hermetic solutions to original equipment manufacturers and defense contractors.

Management emphasizes honest pricing, clear communication, and respect for business contacts as key differentiators, backed by over 100 years of combined experience among its leadership team. The AS9100D certification underscores its quality commitment for aerospace and defense work.
